meta.vaNote: Fourteen validation audits were run after the paper’s analytic freeze and applied to this dataset on October 1–3, 2026, all with an AI system (OpenAI ChatGPT GPT-6 Astra) that took part in the original collection, unblinded; independent human review is pending. (1) A stratified random source recheck of 300 faculty-program records (rank and Scopus h re-searched against institutional pages and authenticated Scopus): rank agreed in 97% of resolvable comparisons and previously matched Scopus profiles agreed in 95% (the differences being one citation accrued since September), but a matching profile with h > 0 was found for 62 of 150 records that had been assigned 0. (2) A recheck of all 83 full-professor listings with a reported Scopus 0: 63 had a profile with h > 0. (3) A recheck of the 329 associate-professor listings with a reported Scopus 0: 66 confirmed discrepancies were transferred and applied. (4–7) A single authenticated author search for each transferred listing with a reported Scopus 0 that remained: 2,262 assistant professors, 614 instructors, 1,787 with no rank and 403 others. Search results are candidates, not confirmed identities, so a candidate was applied only under the dataset’s original matching rule (one name-matched candidate currently affiliated with the person’s own institution, no competing candidate, no truncated result list): 56 listings, 42 of them with h > 0. 2,818 listings with candidates returned remain unresolved (most await a publication-level identity check) and 1,604 searches returned no candidate profile (eleven listings with candidates returned and two with none, fellows, students or administrative support rather than faculty, were removed from the dataset on October 2). Profiles already linked to a record reported as 0 (574) were searched again by name: 494 were reopened, of which 481 still display 0, 10 now display h 1 (one citation accrued since the collection) and were updated to that value, and 3 display a positive value that was not applied (two against the senior author’s explicit adjudication of 0, one where the register’s 0 is a person-level recalculation); 80 were not returned by the search. (8–13) A recheck of the Scopus author profile already linked to every full professor (1,344), associate professor (1,781), assistant professor (2,814), instructor (309), faculty member with no rank (1,056) and emeritus or other-title faculty member (121) with a reported h-index above 0: 7,212 of 7,425 displayed exactly the recorded value (97.1%); the other 213 differed (206 higher, 7 lower; every difference was one point except one decrease of two points); 209 were updated to the displayed value (two of them, a full professor whose linked profile now shows 0 while a second profile of the same physician shows 2 and an assistant professor whose linked profile now shows 4 against 6 recorded while a second profile of the same name shows 3, at the senior author’s decision of October 2, to the higher of the two profiles), 3 more had already been updated by the audit 1 follow-up, and one kept the recorded value: a faculty member with no rank whose linked profile shows 29 against 28 recorded but contains two publications by other authors, so that the value recalculated without them (28) was confirmed. The five previously audited profiles that displayed one point more than the recorded value were updated by the same rule (214 updates in all). Second profiles of the same name were screened for the full and associate professors only (the assistant-professor, instructor, no-rank and emeritus/other files carry no candidate list). These rechecks confirm the displayed value of the linked profile, not that the profile belongs to the person. (14) A record-by-record authenticated author search (full name, then first initial; up to ten candidates captured) of the 471 listings with a reported 0 that no earlier audit file covered (261 associate professors, 208 assistant professors, 1 emeritus listing and one fellowship director added after the freeze): the AI system proposed 53 profiles with h > 0 and 51 matched profiles displaying 0, found no author for 38 and left 329 unresolved. Every proposed profile was checked against the person’s publications (PubMed) and institutional pages before it was applied: of the 53, 21 were confirmed, 1 was replaced by the correct profile (the proposed one was another person of the same name), 5 that could not be established were kept at 0 unless confirmed (senior author, October 3) and 26 were rejected (25 belonged to another person, 1 was not supported by the evidence); of the 51 at 0, 42 were the linked profile reconfirmed, 6 were confirmed new matches and 3 belonged to another person. With two more profiles confirmed among the unresolved candidates, 23 listings now carry an observed h-index above 0 (1 to 17, median 3) and 7 an observed 0, and 356 assigned zeros with candidates keep their value with a caution (323 unresolved, 28 whose selected profile was rejected, 5 held). The 251 recovered values replaced assigned or observed zeros, 27 recovered profiles displaying 0 are now observed zeros, 22 completed negative searches of audits 1 and 2 are labelled as such, the 38 audit-14 searches that returned no author are recorded with the zero kept, 8 ranks were set to the current official source, and unresolved cases keep their value with a caution. An assigned 0 means that no profile was found at collection, not that the person has no publications: 4,832 assigned zeros remain, and the recovered counts are floors on the false zeros, not estimates of them (in the random sample a matching profile with h > 0 was found for 41% of the assigned zeros). Every listing now carries an audit disposition, shown on its faculty record. Separately from the h-index audits, the academic rank of every listing was re-examined against current institutional pages (rank re-audits R1 to R6, October 2–3: full professor 1,368, associate professor 2,058, assistant professor 5,622, instructor 920, no rank 2,827, emeritus and other titles 162 listings): of 12,934 distinct listings, 6,797 ranks were confirmed as recorded, 51 were changed (four to emeritus; six University of Virginia listings recorded as emeritus whose own profiles show active ranks, four associate and two assistant professors; six promotions to full professor, thirteen promotions to associate professor, six to assistant professor, fourteen University of Chicago clinical associates recorded in the non-ladder category other, and two changes to no rank; ten of the promotions took effect on October 1, 2026, after the collection window), eleven titles were refined within the same category (for example adjunct lecturer), sixteen listings were removed (one administrative-support listing, fourteen fellows or students listed with the faculty, and one listing of a physician who died in 2023), 36 with conflicting current sources keep the recorded rank with a flag and 6,023 whose rank could not be independently re-read keep the recorded rank. A scan for the same person listed twice at the same institution (same Scopus profile) found seven duplicate listings, which were removed (October 3).

M.D./M.H.S. is an Assistant Professor of Emergency Medicine at the Boston University Chobanian and Avedisian School of Medicine, the Medical Director for the ED-Addiction Consult Team, and the Associate Medical Director of Faster Paths to Treatment, Boston Medical Center's low-barrier addiction bridge clinic. She graduated cum laude from the Yale School of Medicine and completed her residency training in Emergency Medicine and Addiction Medicine fellowship at Boston Medical Center. Dr. Weisenthal is an active researcher in the fields of Emergency and Addiction Medicine. Her areas of interest include program implementation to improve initiation and access to evidence-based medications for substance use disorder in the Emergency Department, ensuring smooth transitions of care from the emergency to outpatient settings, and integrating a harm reduction and trauma-informed approach into Emergency Department patient care.
